Born: February 11, 1969, 10:22 PM local time, Los Angeles, California, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or birth record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be taken at face value. Open Jennifer Aniston's chart on Astrolas alongside this read.

This chart pairs almost every planet off by house. The Sun and Mercury share the 4th house in Aquarius. Venus and Saturn share the 6th house in Aries. The Moon, Mars and Neptune all land in the 2nd house. And Jupiter and Uranus sit together in the 12th house in Libra, in the one conjunction tight enough for the Astrolas library to have a direct reading on.

That last pair describes a kind of luck that works quietly, through other people and behind the scenes, rather than through loud effort. It is a fair description of a career that includes one of the most famous casting-timing stories in television: she had already signed on to a different, short-lived CBS pilot before being released to join the cast of Friends in 1994.

muc.ten: Jupiter conjunct Uranus in Libra, house 12: luck that works through other people
doan: Jupiter sits at 5°15' Libra and Uranus at 3°28' Libra, both in the 12th house, conjunct with an orb of 1°47'.

The Astrolas library reads this pairing as a willingness to take risks that keeps paying off: being in the right place at the right time, benefiting from unexpected opportunities, and finding that lasting luck tends to arrive through relationships rather than through solo effort. It adds that knowing the right people at the right moment is often the real key to the opening.

Friends ran for ten seasons, from 1994 to 2004, and turned its six leads into some of the best-paid actors on television after they negotiated their contracts together rather than separately. The 12th house keeps this kind of fortune out of the spotlight. In recent years that has included producing work through her company Echo Films, among them an executive producer credit on Apple TV+'s The Morning Show, where she also stars as Alex Levy.

muc.ten: Sun and Mercury in Aquarius, house 4: the home as the project
doan: The Sun sits at 23°22' Aquarius and Mercury at 0°27' Aquarius, both in the 4th house.

The library reads this Sun as original, independent-minded and future-facing, more drawn to ideas than to status, with a wide circle of friends and a mind that runs ahead of the moment. In the 4th house, that same placement turns toward home and roots: the library describes a devoted family member whose home becomes a showcase for creative work, decorating, renovating and collecting, and who enjoys hosting people in it. Mercury in Aquarius adds original, independent thinking and a liking for ideas that others haven't gotten to yet; in the 4th house, the library notes a mind that stays busy inside the house itself, sometimes running a project or a small business from home.

Aniston's homes have been public property for years, repeatedly featured and renovated, down to the design choices. The chart's reading of Aquarius in the 4th house, creativity expressed through the house itself, fits that pattern closely.

muc.ten: Venus and Saturn in Aries, house 6: work, discipline and one well-known romance
doan: Venus sits at 9°13' Aries and Saturn at 21°08' Aries, both in the 6th house.

The library reads Venus in Aries as love that arrives fast and intensely, drawn first by chemistry, and warns against spending just as quickly. In the 6th house, it adds a detail worth noting here: romantic opportunities sometimes arrive through colleagues. Aniston and Justin Theroux worked together on Wanderlust, released in 2012, and started dating not long after; they married in 2015. Saturn in Aries describes ambition mixed with early obstacles that build resilience over time, well suited to starting an independent venture; in the 6th house, it becomes a strong, disciplined work ethic that keeps personal life and the job in separate boxes. She launched LolaVie, a hair care line, in 2021.

muc.ten: The Moon in Sagittarius, Mars and Neptune in Scorpio, all in the 2nd house
doan: Three planets share the 2nd house, the Astrolas library's house of money and resources, though they arrive in it from three different signs. The Moon sits at 23°16' Sagittarius, Mars at 23°50' Scorpio and Neptune at 28°38' Scorpio.

The library's Moon in Sagittarius wants emotional freedom and resists feeling tied down, and in the 2nd house that shows up as linking security to accumulation while still spending freely when restless. Mars in Scorpio brings intense, focused drive and real staying power once committed; in the 2nd house, the library notes real entrepreneurial talent paired with a need for a clear plan before any major financial move. Neptune in Scorpio is also a generational placement, shared by everyone born in roughly the same years, pulling toward hidden depths and transformation on a societal scale; in the 2nd house it becomes personal as sharp financial intuition mixed with a tendency to lose track of money in ways that are hard to explain, plus a strong emotional pull toward objects and keepsakes tied to memory.

muc.ten: Pluto in Virgo, house 11: a generational marker, personal through friendship
doan: Pluto sits at 24°33' Virgo in the 11th house. By sign, Pluto in Virgo is generational, shared by everyone born between 1957 and 1971, a cohort the library ties to civil rights and labor reform on a broad scale. The personal story here runs through the house.

The library ties an 11th-house Pluto to real influence inside groups, often exercised quietly: attracting powerful or complicated friendships, and reshaping an organization's structure from behind the scenes rather than by taking the podium. It calls this kind of person a "silent catalyst," someone whose impact in a group becomes clear only after it has already happened.

The Friends cast negotiation fits this closely. Rather than any one actor striking a bigger deal, all six stood together and renegotiated as a single unit, eventually earning roughly $1 million per episode each by the show's final seasons, a move that reset the economics of the entire industry.

muc.ten: Libra rising, and the angles still outside the library
doan: The Ascendant sits at 24°40' Libra, with the Descendant at 24°40' Aries, the Midheaven at 27°19' Cancer and the IC at 27°19' Capricorn. With an AA-rated time, these can be read with confidence, but the Astrolas library doesn't yet have entries for any of the four angles themselves, so this piece doesn't build a reading on them directly.

A handful of aspects touch the angles too: the Sun trine the Ascendant (orb 1°17'), the Moon sextile the Ascendant (orb 1°24'), and Mercury opposite the Midheaven (orb 3°08'). None of them have library text yet either, so they stay here as chart facts rather than a reading.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: The chart doesn't explain thirty years of steady work on screen. What it does show is a pattern worth noticing: almost every planet in this chart pairs off inside one house, and the one pairing the library actually speaks to, Jupiter and Uranus in the 12th, reads as luck that moves through relationships and shows up behind the scenes rather than in the spotlight.
